examples.en: I jumped from the plane wearing a parachute.
Once the parachute opened, I began to come down slowly.
I attached a parachute to the box and dropped it.
The rescue team sent supplies down by parachute.
Parachute training is very dangerous.
The kids played a parachute game on the playground.

explain: 비행기에서 뛰어내릴 때 쓰는 도구예요. 한국어에서는 여기서 나온 '낙하산 인사'라는 말이 더 자주 들려요. 실력이 아니라 연줄로 높은 자리에 오른 사람을 부정적으로 말할 때 써요.

phrases.example: 새 사장이 낙하산 인사라서 직원들이 불만이 많아요.
phrases.nuance_ko: 실력이 아닌 연줄로 높은 자리에 간 사람을 비판할 때 써요. 대부분 부정적인 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used critically for someone placed in a high position through connections rather than merit. It is almost always negative.

explain_en: It is the equipment used when jumping from an airplane. In Korean, the derived phrase '낙하산 인사' is heard even more often, a negative term for someone placed in a high post through connections rather than ability.

examples.en: Grandfather cuts the grass with a sickle.
A sickle has a sharp blade, so you must be careful.

examples.ko: 농사를 짓는 분들은 낫을 자주 써요.
examples.en: People who farm often use sickles.
A sickle hangs in the storage shed of the country house.
I bought a new sickle.

examples.ko: 벼를 낫으로 베던 시절 이야기를 들었어요.
examples.en: I heard a story about the days when rice was cut with sickles.

explain: 풀이나 곡식을 베는, 끝이 굽은 농기구예요. 소리가 같은 '낫다'(병이 나아지다, 더 좋다)와 헷갈리지 않게 문장 속 쓰임을 봐야 해요. 낫은 '낫이, 낫을, 낫으로'처럼 받침 ㅅ이 다음 소리로 넘어가요.
explain_en: It's the farm tool with a curved blade for cutting grass or grain. Don't confuse it with the verb 낫다 (to get better, to be better), which sounds the same; context tells them apart. With particles the ㅅ carries over, as in 낫이, 낫을, 낫으로.

examples.en: The bike had rusted, so I wiped it.

examples.ko: 비를 맞은 못에 녹이 많이 생겼어요.
examples.en: A lot of rust formed on the nails that got rained on.
If you spray rust remover, it comes off easily.
The old key was covered in rust.

examples.ko: 칼에 녹이 슬지 않게 물기를 닦아 두세요.
examples.en: Wipe off the moisture so the knife doesn't rust.

examples.ko: 다리 난간에 붉은 녹이 올라와 있었어요.
examples.en: Red rust had come up on the bridge railing.

explain: '녹이 슬다'가 가장 자연스러운 짝이에요. 쇠가 녹는다는 뜻의 '녹다'와 소리가 비슷하지만 전혀 다른 말이에요. 쇠로 된 물건에만 쓰고, 오래 안 써서 둔해진 걸 '녹슬다'로도 말해요.
explain_en: The natural pairing is '녹이 슬다'. It sounds like the verb '녹다' (to melt) but is a different word. It's for metal things, and '녹슬다' is also used for skills that have gone dull from lack of use.

examples.en: Grandfather reads the newspaper wearing reading glasses.

examples.ko: 돋보기로 보면 곤충의 날개가 자세히 보여요.
examples.en: With a magnifying glass, you can see an insect's wings in detail.
My eyesight got worse, so I started to need reading glasses.
The researcher looked through a magnifying glass all day.

examples.ko: 작은 글씨는 돋보기 없이 못 읽어요.
examples.en: I can't read small print without reading glasses.

examples.ko: 돋보기 앱을 켜면 스마트폰으로 글씨를 키울 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you open a magnifier app, you can enlarge text on your smartphone.

explain: 작은 것을 크게 보는 렌즈도 '돋보기'이고, 나이가 들어 가까운 글씨가 안 보일 때 쓰는 안경도 '돋보기'라고 해요. 안경을 분명히 말할 때는 '돋보기안경'이라고도 해요. 스마트폰의 확대 기능도 '돋보기'라고 불러요.
explain_en: A lens that enlarges small things is a '돋보기', and so are the glasses people wear when close-up text gets hard to see with age. To make clear it's glasses, people also say '돋보기안경'. The zoom feature on smartphones is called '돋보기' too.

examples.en: I read a book in front of the living room fireplace.
I put firewood in the fireplace.
I want to live in a house with a fireplace.

examples.ko: 눈 오는 날 벽난로 불빛이 따뜻해 보여요.
examples.en: The fireplace light looks warm on a snowy day.

examples.ko: 아이들이 벽난로 앞에 모여 이야기를 들어요.
examples.en: The kids gather in front of the fireplace and listen to a story.
Apartments these days almost never have a fireplace.

explain: 한국의 전통 집에는 온돌이 있어서 벽난로는 서양 영화나 펜션에서 더 자주 봐요. '벽난로에 불을 피우다', '벽난로 앞에 앉다'처럼 써요.
explain_en: Traditional Korean houses have ondol floor heating, so fireplaces are more often seen in Western movies or pensions. You say '벽난로에 불을 피우다' and '벽난로 앞에 앉다'.

examples.ko: 태풍 뒤에 마을 사람들이 길을 복구했어요.
examples.en: After the typhoon the villagers restored the road.
I want to recover the file I deleted.
The technician restored the internet quickly for me.

examples.ko: 다리를 복구하는 데 일 년이 걸렸어요.
examples.en: It took a year to repair the bridge.
I'm glad the restored photo looks just like before.
To recover data, first look for the backup.

explain: 고장 나거나 부서진 것을 원래 상태로 되돌리는 일에 써요. 컴퓨터 파일, 도로, 전기처럼 큰 피해를 고칠 때 많이 말해요. 작은 물건을 고치는 일에는 '고치다'를 써요. '복원하다'는 옛 모습을 되살리는 느낌이에요.
explain_en: It is for bringing something broken or damaged back to its original state, often for big damage such as computer files, roads, or power. For small objects use 고치다. 복원하다 feels like reviving an old appearance.

examples.en: A small bird is singing inside the birdcage.

examples.ko: 새장 문을 열어 두었더니 새가 날아갔어요.
examples.en: I left the birdcage door open and the bird flew away.
I hung the birdcage by the sunny window.

examples.ko: 아이가 새장에 모이를 넣어 주고 있어요.
examples.en: The child is putting feed into the birdcage.

examples.ko: 새장이 너무 작아서 새가 불편해 보여요.
examples.en: The birdcage is so small that the bird looks uncomfortable.

examples.ko: 새장 청소는 일주일에 한 번 해요.
examples.en: I clean the birdcage once a week.

explain: '새장'은 사람이 새를 기르려고 가두는 곳이라, 새가 직접 짓는 '둥지'나 새를 위해 달아 주는 '새집'과 달라요. '새장 속의 새'처럼 자유가 없는 처지를 비유하기도 해요.
explain_en: A '새장' is where people keep a bird, unlike a '둥지' (nest) that birds build or a '새집' (birdhouse) put up for them. A phrase like '새장 속의 새' figuratively describes someone without freedom.

examples.en: I set up a support pole for the tent to block the wind.
I stuck a stake in next to the plant pot.
This shelf wobbles because its braces are weak.
I propped up my injured arm with a brace.

examples.ko: 공사장 지지대가 쓰러지지 않게 단단히 고정했어요.
examples.en: I fixed the supports at the construction site firmly so they would not fall.
Working with a back brace on is comfortable.

explain: '지지대'는 텐트, 화분, 선반처럼 눈에 보이는 물건을 받치는 도구에만 써요. '지지하다'와 뿌리가 같은 말이라서 함께 기억하면 쉬워요. 사람이나 힘이 되는 존재를 비유할 때는 '버팀목'이라는 말을 써요.
explain_en: 지지대 is only used for physical things that hold up an object, like tent poles, plant stakes and shelf braces. It shares a root with 지지하다, which can help you remember it. For a person or force that supports someone figuratively, the word is 버팀목.
